title: 2028 Volvo XC90: Prices, Reviews & Pictures - CarGurus.com
summary: Explore the 2028 Volvo XC90 with CarGurus reviews, pricing insights, comparisons, news and expert analysis.
body_markdown:
## Look & feel


8/10


The Volvo XC90 is handsome, with strong horizontal lines and minimalist interior styling. The lighter materials included in our test vehicle gave an open and airy feel to the cabin that evokes a sense of calm. We liked the elegant use of ambient lighting that highlights the premium materials inside the cabin rather than turning the interior into a futuristic discotheque. The overall effect of the materials and accents is traditional yet modern, not garish.


During our test drive in Copenhagen, Denmark, we had access to the top-tier Ultra trim with the tailored dash and Cardamom leather interior. There is close attention to detail throughout the cabin with stitching accents on the seats and piping on the dash materials. The hand-blown Orrefors crystal shift knob is one of those unique accents that's next-level luxurious and great to grip. The use of aluminum on the dash and speaker vents ties together the overall premium look and feel of the XC90, and we particularly liked the etched metal edges on the knobs and dials.


The one potentially polarizing interior design feature is the large vertical screen mounted on the center stack. It pops off the dash slightly, making it look more like an iPad glued to the dash rather than being integrated with the center stack. It is tilted slightly toward the driver for better access, and the screen is flanked by vertical air vents, which makes it feel more like a conscious design element rather than an afterthought. Those who like their tech will appreciate the large on-screen icons and general design simplicity with minimal buttons and dials.


## Performance


6/10


The B5 and B6 powertrains carry over into the 2028 Volvo XC90 with their 2.0-liter four-cylinder turbocharged and supercharged engines. They are both mild hybrids, delivering 247 and 295 horsepower, respectively. The big change for 2028 comes to the T8 model, which gets a larger 41.2-kWh lithium-ion battery. This ups the range from 32 miles to 73 miles in 2028. The same 2.0-liter turbo-four in the B5 and B6 underpins the T8 and is essentially the same as the previous model year, but the 2028 model gets a more powerful rear motor. So, the 455-hp total output remains the same, but combined torque gets a slight boost to 560 pound-feet. All models in this lineup come standard with all-wheel drive and an eight-speed automatic transmission.


One of the biggest selling points for the XC90 is the smooth and comfortable ride combined with the quietness of the cabin. Since Scandinavian roads are generally very good, we didn’t get to do our typical pothole and speed-bump tests in this specific model, but we have in previous model years. The comfort results for the XC90 are well above those of sportier vehicles such as the BMW X5 and Audi Q7.


We were less impressed with the power from the plug-in hybrid powertrain in our test vehicle, because the performance is much more sluggish than the numbers imply. We toggled through the various drive options from Hybrid to Power to Pure and noticed a similar lag from a stop. We expected the instantaneous torque of the PHEV powertrain to kick in, especially in Pure mode, but it didn’t. For those who aren't aggressive drivers, this might not be something they’ll care about or notice. However, there were times when we missed the boost we thought we’d get with this powertrain; passing maneuvers on the highway were fine but not especially zippy.


## Form & function


7/10


The Volvo XC90 is a seven-passenger, three-row midsize SUV, packed with a lot of family-friendly, practical features. First, we love that Volvo doesn’t try to squish three passengers in the third row, especially since legroom is already at a premium, and we appreciate the decent access to the third row with tilt-and-slide second-row seats. But the most practical feature is the integrated booster seat in the second-row middle seat on models with bench seating. The booster is there on demand but magically disappears when transporting adults or older children.


While the cargo space for the XC90 is less than most of its competitors behind all rows, its boxy shape offers more usable space as well as some underfloor storage behind the third row for small items. Plus, there are some great practical features in the back, including the standard power liftgate, 12-volt cargo-area outlet, and available lowering rear suspension, which makes loading heavy luggage or pets a lot easier.


Other great standard features include the netted pockets on the back of the front seats, quad-zone climate controls, heated front seats, third-row air vents, power child safety locks, rain-sensing windshield wipers, and a plethora of cup holders. A few available features we’d recommend include power-folding side mirrors, rear sunshades, and heated washer nozzles. Oh, and on the Ultra trim, buyers can look forward to front-seat massagers.


## Technology


8/10


As part of the refresh in 2025, the XC90 got a larger 11.2-inch screen, which makes it easier to access all the vehicle functions, including climate controls, located within said screen. But the biggest, and we’d argue best, tech feature in the 2028 model is the addition of Gemini AI. In addition to natural voice commands for navigation, it also lets drivers adjust the likes of temperature and seat heaters without needing to touch the screen. Plus, if drivers are trying to figure out how to do something in the vehicle, such as change drive modes, Gemini can access the owner’s manual and tell them how to do it, so there’s no need to read the manual.


Gemini can also answer non-car questions. For example, during our test in Copenhagen, we passed a fortification that had cannons facing the water, and we were curious about it. Gemini was able to give us the name of the fort and explain its historical significance. This is a part of Google built-in, and the AI features come with a four-year trial.


Outside of Gemini, there are a lot of great standard and available tech features on the 2028 XC90, but we think it's odd that the standard Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are still of the wired variety—even when there is a standard wireless phone charger. Other standard tech features starting on the Core trim include a 12.3-inch digital cluster, four USB-C ports, and a 10-speaker high-performance audio system. The mid-tier Plus trim adds features such as a 14-speaker Harman Kardon audio system, a surround-view camera system, headlight washers, and sound-insulated side windows. The Ultra trim brings standard features such as the head-up display, ventilated front seats, and additional power seat adjustments as well as available features such as the Bowers & Wilkins premium audio system, front-seat massagers, and air suspension.


## Safety


9/10


Even the base Core trim is packed with standard safety and driver-assistance features—just as we'd expect from Volvo. Every XC90 comes with adaptive cruise control, blind-spot monitors, lane-keep assist, front and rear parking sensors, automatic emergency braking, rear cross-traffic alert, automatic reverse braking, and traffic-sign recognition. The Plus trim adds a surround-view camera and side sensors, and at the top-tier Ultra trim, buyers also get a head-up display.


At the time of writing, neither the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) nor the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) had crash tested the 2028 XC90. But the IIHS gave the 2026 XC90 a Top Safety Pick designation with all Good crashworthiness scores and a mix of Good and Acceptable crash avoidance and mitigation scores. The NHTSA gave the 2027 XC90 a five-star overall safety rating.


Since we were in the Ultra trim, we had access to all the safety tech, and one of our favorite features was the surround-view camera that gives measurements to how close the car is to an obstacle. When we were backing into a space, it said we were 23 cm away from a hedge. Since we had a tape measure, we double-checked the measurement, and it was spot on. Thankfully, we didn’t have the chance to test most of the other safety features, but we will say that the traffic-sign recognition system's information isn’t always accurate. There were a couple of times we were in a 50 km/h (30 mph) zone, and the system was reading 80 km/h (50 mph).


## Cost-effectiveness


7/10


The 2028 Volvo XC90 is due out in the first quarter of 2027, and Volvo execs said pricing will be available closer to the time of launch, but we can make some general assumptions about cost effectiveness based on current pricing. Assessing the three-row competitive set that includes the Lexus TX, the Audi Q7, the Genesis GV80, the Acura MDX, and the Infiniti QX60, the XC90 is not the obvious value leader. Looking at base models, it sits at the top of the price spectrum, as only the Q7 costs more.


However, the XC90 has a lot of standard features that cost extra on other vehicles—if they’re even available. That includes the likes of all-wheel drive, a panoramic sunroof, four-zone climate control, heated front seats, Matrix LED headlights, and a built-in booster seat. A feature-matched price comparison is more interesting, because the XC90 becomes one of the lower-cost vehicles in the set, with only the Infiniti QX60 having a lower price tag in this respect.


While we think the Core trim of the XC90 is very well equipped, we’d opt for the Plus trim simply because we really want (and recommend) the surround-view camera. No matter the powertrain, this trim adds about $4,000 to the bottom line, and we think it’s worth every penny. As far as powertrains are concerned, that depends on the buyer's particular needs and wants. For those who don’t need a lot of power, the 247-hp B5 powertrain will be fine, but more aggressive drivers will want the 295-hp B6 powertrain. EV-curious buyers who aren’t quite ready to take the plunge should go for the new long-range T8.


Looking at the Plus trim for each powertrain, 2028 pricing will likely start at around $67,000 for the B5 and $71,000 for the B6, and the T8 will probably exceed $81,000. It’s also worth noting that the 2028 T8 does not offer a Core trim, so for buyers who want the PHEV powertrain, Plus is the base model.
